before.text:
By writing ζ(γ + it) = |ζ(γ + it)| exp(−iθγ (t)), we see that all the information about the
zeros along the t−axis is contained in the phase θγ (t). This has to jump by π to accomodate
the sign change in ζ at every zero, and it can be shown that the oscillating part of the
density of the zeros on the critical line is proportional to the derivative of the imaginry part
of ln ζ(t) with respect to t [10]. On the other hand, we see from Eq. (2) that the appropriate
contour integral over ln ζ(β) also yields ρ(x) relating to the primes. Thus, the phase of the
zeta function, as defined above, connects the Riemann zeros to the primes.

experiment is to move the zeros off the critical line, that is, to arbitrarily change their real
parts. We find this still produces lines at the primes and their powers, but the relative
intensities are incorrect. This is interesting since it demonstrates that the location of the
primes depends only on the imaginary part of the zero. The real part only affects the
intensities which are anyway not evident from a direct evaluation of the series. This provides
another motivation for the numerical and analytical procedures described in this paper.

after.text:
With regard to spectral statistics, it is well known that nearest-neighbour spacings (NNS)
[19] of the Riemann zeros obey the GUE distribution of Random Matrix Theory, character-
istic of a chaotic quantum system without time-reversal symmetry [20, 21]. The same zeros
also generate the spectrum of the primes and their powers through Riemann’s formula (3).
As mentioned earlier, the NNS distribution of the primes is Poisson-like [8], with some level
repulsion, which, if at all of dynamic origin, hints only to near-integrability [1]. Thus, it is
quite remarkable that the highly-correlated sequence of the zeros can (through Riemann’s
formula) interfere to produce the almost-uncorrelated sequence of the primes.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The trace-formula analogy fails a structural audit: an action-like phase is not enough without repetition structure, orbit-dependent amplitudes, and a single dynamics that consistently generates both smooth and oscillatory energy dependence.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source tests the identifications of alpha as an orbit label, x as energy, and alpha log x as an action. It rejects a dynamical trace-formula reading because there are no repetition indices, the implied orbits are not periodic, amplitudes have no alpha dependence, and one Hamiltonian is unlikely to generate both the oscillatory denominator and smooth term consistently.
directed.conceptual_reading: A valid representation bridge must preserve the compositional structure of its target, not merely its cosine form. Periodic-orbit semantics require primitive orbits and repetitions, stability-sensitive weights, and compatible smooth and fluctuating components.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The candidate bridge maps zero-indexed oscillations to trajectory contributions in a density of states; missing dynamical invariants provide the obstruction.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The conclusion rules out Riemann's formula as a trace formula of dynamical origin under these criteria, not every possible Hamiltonian with prime spectrum. A separate footnote also limits which smooth term could be Thomas-Fermi data.
directed.uncertainty: Low for the source's explicit structural objections; the claim that no fortuitous cancellation can repair all energy dependence is argued as unlikely rather than formally impossible.

supported: The span tests alpha as orbit label, x as energy, and alpha log x as action, then identifies absent repetition indices, nonperiodic implied orbits, alpha-independent amplitudes, and incompatible energy dependence as obstructions.
Its final conclusion is specifically that Riemann's formula is not a trace formula of dynamical origin, with one consistency argument stated as unlikely rather than impossible.
inference: Requiring compositional orbit structure rather than cosine-form resemblance is a strong non-paraphrase synthesis of the explicit objections.
unsupported_or_imported: The phrase 'stability-sensitive weights' imports a standard semiclassical detail not stated in this span, which only requires orbit-dependent amplitudes.
The separate trivial-zero footnote is outside this unit's exact span and should not be presented as support inside this candidate.
